summary: Build JSON.stringify's ordered de-duplicated property list from a replacer array, including its non-enumerability and inheritance effects.

target.notes: Only String/Number primitives and boxed String/Number entries contribute property names after ToString, in first-occurrence order. For objects this PropertyList is used directly, so selected non-enumerable or inherited names can be serialized.

semantics.accepted_entries: String and Number primitives plus boxed String/Number values
semantics.order: PropertyList order controls serialized object member order
semantics.enumerability: PropertyList lookup is not limited to own enumerable properties
semantics.inherited: Get can serialize an inherited selected property
semantics.arrays: PropertyList does not filter array indices; arrays serialize their indexed elements

caveats: Using Object.keys(value).Where(replacerContains) is wrong: it loses replacer order and cannot include inherited/non-enumerable selected properties.

tests.name: can include nonenumerable and inherited selected names
tests.input: const p={x:7}; const o=Object.create(p); Object.defineProperty(o,'y',{value:8}); o.z=9; console.log(JSON.stringify(o,['y','x']));
